source.title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Construct the ultraviolet limit of the two-dimensional O(N) nonlinear sigma model, viewed here as an asymptotically free bosonic field theory.

evidence.quote: Construct the ultraviolet limit of the two dimensional O(N) non linear sigma model, which is a well behaved asymptotically free bosonic field theory

accepted.question_text: Construct the finite-volume correlation functions of four-dimensional Yang-Mills theory in a standard gauge such as Landau gauge, which the paper says likely requires a direct treatment of the Gribov problem.

evidence.quote: Construct the Yang Mills 4 correlation functions in a finite volume and a standard gauge (such as the Landau gauge). This presumably implies a front attack on the Gribov problem.

accepted.question_text: Simplify and rewrite Balaban's lattice gauge theory results into a more accessible constructive account.

evidence.quote: Simplify and rewrite Balaban’s results on the lattice gauge theory. This is no small task since references in [Ba1] total hundreds of pages.

accepted.question_text: Clarify the nature of the renormalized perturbation series for four-dimensional φ⁴ theory, including proving that renormalons really occur.

evidence.quote: Elucidate the nature of φ4 4 renormalized pertubation series, proving for instance that renormalons do exist

accepted.question_text: Prove in full generality that the ultraviolet limit of four-dimensional φ⁴ theory is trivial.

evidence.quote: Can one prove in full generality that its ultraviolet limit is trivial

accepted.question_text: Develop constructive versions of supersymmetric and topological field theories, including a constructive understanding of Montonen-Olive duality for N = 4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills in four dimensions and Seiberg-Witten duality for N = 2 supersymmetric Yang-Mills in four dimensions.

evidence.quote: Develop constructive versions of the now-popular supersymmetric field theories, and topological field theories: develop a constructive understanding of Montonen-Olive duality in N = 4 SUSY Yang-Mills4, and of Seiberg-Witten duality for N = 2 SUSY Yang-Mills4.

accepted.question_text: Glue the ultraviolet analysis of the Gross-Neveu model to its non-perturbative mass generation analysis at large N in order to obtain a constructive example of dimensional transmutation.

evidence.quote: Glue the ultraviolet analysis of the Gross-Neveu model [GK1][FMRS][DR1] with the non-perturbative mass generation of the same model [KMR] at large N, to obtain the first example of so called dimensional transmutation.

accepted.question_text: Glue the ultraviolet construction of the large-N φ⁴ theory in three dimensions to the infrared analysis of continuous symmetry breaking so as to control the continuous-symmetry-broken phase without an ultraviolet cutoff.

evidence.quote: One could also glue the ultraviolet construction of φ4 3 to the infrared continuous symmetry breaking analysis of [Ba2] to control the large N-component φ4 3 model in the continuous symmetry broken phase without an ultraviolet cutoff.

accepted.question_text: Prove that the phase transition of two-dimensional φ⁴ theory lies in the same universality class, with the same critical exponents, as the two-dimensional Ising phase transition.

evidence.quote: the first significant result should be to prove that the phase transition of φ4 2 is in the same universality class (i.e. has the same critical exponents) than the Ising 2 phase transition.

accepted.question_text: For each conformal field theory in the ADE family that arises as the scaling limit of an integrable lattice model, find a corresponding model that can actually be constructed by constructive methods.

evidence.quote: there exist integrable lattice models of the ADE type which scale to conformal field theories of the [BPZ] classification at their critical point [Pa]; can we find a model which can be built with constructive methods for every such conformal theory?

accepted.question_text: Develop phase-space analysis and non-perturbative methods for quantum field theory directly in Minkowski space, with the goal of obtaining the first proofs of asymptotic completeness for quantum field theory models.

evidence.quote: Develop phase space analysis and non-perturbative methods for field theory that work directly in Minkowski space. This should lead to first proofs of asymptotic completeness

accepted.question_text: Complete in full detail the construction of the three-dimensional Gross-Neveu model with a large number of components, and construct analogous non-renormalizable models such as the corresponding regime of the sine-Gordon model.

evidence.quote: Complete in full detail the construction of the first non renormalizable field theory, the Gross-Neveu model in three dimensions and large number of components [dCFdVMS][dV]. Construct other models of this type, for instance the corresponding regime of the sine-Gordon model.

accepted.question_text: Develop constructive field theory in curved space-time.

evidence.quote: Develop constructive field theory in curved space-time.

accepted.question_text: Make substantially better contact between constructive field theory and the C*-algebra or algebraic-field-theory approach, including the renormalization-group viewpoint in that setting.

evidence.quote: Make better contact with the C∗-algebra approach (sometimes called axiomatic field theory). We refer to [BV] for a point of view on the renormalization group in algebraic field theory.

accepted.question_text: Find a direct proof of convergence of the Mayer expansion for dipoles at low activity, without relying on a cluster expansion, for a dipole-dipole interaction smoothed at short distance so that it is stable.

evidence.quote: Find a direct proof of convergence of the Mayer expansion for dipoles at low activity (which does not use a cluster expansion). The dipole-dipole interaction should be smoothed at short distance so that it is stable.

accepted.question_text: Prove convergence of the Mayer expansion at low activity in the Kosterlitz-Thouless phase of the two-dimensional Coulomb gas, presumably through an effective multipole analysis.

evidence.quote: Convergence of the Mayer expansion at low activity for the KT phase of the 2D Coulomb gas. This is harder than the previous problem, and involves presumably an effective analysis of that gas in terms of multipoles.

accepted.question_text: Prove exponential screening in the two-dimensional Coulomb gas at temperatures that are not especially small, possibly all the way down to the Kosterlitz-Thouless transition.

evidence.quote: Prove exponential screening in the 2D Coulomb gas at not particularly small temperatures (down to the KT transition?).

accepted.question_text: Control the correlations at the Kosterlitz-Thouless transition.

evidence.quote: Control the correlations at the KT transition.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the transitions between βKT and 1/2βKT in the two-dimensional Coulomb gas are visible in any correlation functions.

evidence.quote: Are the transitions between βKT and 1/2βKT in the D=2 Coulomb gas visible in any correlations?

accepted.question_text: In the two-dimensional Anderson model at weak coupling, prove that the model is always localized with localization length exponentially small as the coupling tends to zero, beginning with a proof that a single averaged Green's function decays on the λ^-2 scale and then analyzing <G+G-> for localization.

evidence.quote: It is expected that the Anderson 2 model And2 is always localized but with exponentially small localization length when the coupling constant tends to 0. A proof of this statement through constructive field theory methods seems to require first the proof of decay of a single averaged Green’s function < G± > on a scale proportional to λ−2, the square of the coupling constant

accepted.question_text: In the three-dimensional Anderson model at small coupling, prove the expected diffusive phase and the insulating-to-conducting Anderson-Mott phase transition by first controlling the averaged Green's function on the λ^-2 length scale and then the square modulus <G+G->.

evidence.quote: In dimension 3 one expects the small coupling phase to be diffusive, hence the system should undergo an “Anderson Mott” phase transition from insulating to conducting at a certain critical coupling. To prove this one should again first control the decay on a length scale of λ−2 of a single averaged Green’s function

accepted.question_text: Give a constructive solution of spin-glass models such as the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model, including a correct notion of states and an understanding of the ultrametric structure conjectured by physicists.

evidence.quote: To “solve” in a constructive sense models like the Sherrington-Kirckpatrik model is certainly an ambitious goal for the future. One should understand the correct notion of states for the model (in particular in connexion with the ultrametric structure conjectured by the physicists).

accepted.question_text: Understand Parisi's replica symmetry breaking tool in a more precise and constructive way.

evidence.quote: It would be fascinating to also understand in a more precise and constructive sense the replica symmetry breaking tool of Parisi.

accepted.question_text: For polymers with partly attractive but stable small interactions, prove that they scale to Brownian motion in dimensions greater than 4, and determine whether phase transitions exist when the interaction is stable but attractive.

evidence.quote: Polymers with partly attractive interactions: prove that they scale to Brownian motion in d > 4, at least if the interaction is stable and small. Existence of transitions when the interaction is stable but attractive?

accepted.question_text: Find new proofs that the end-to-end distance of the four-dimensional self-avoiding walk has exponent 1/2 with logarithmic corrections.

evidence.quote: d = 4 Self avoiding walk: find new proofs that the end-to-end distance has an exponent of 1/2 with log corrections.

accepted.question_text: Find new proofs that random walk in random environment scales to Brownian motion in dimensions greater than 2.

evidence.quote: Find new proofs that random walk in random environment scales to Brownian motion in d > 2.

accepted.question_text: Prove nontrivial results about the expected end-to-end distance of a self-avoiding walk in dimensions below 4, including whether it exceeds that of simple random walk, whether it has an exponent, and whether that exponent differs from 1/2.

evidence.quote: Prove anything at all about the expected end-to end distance of a self avoiding walk in d < 4. Is it greater than that of simple random walk? Does it have an exponent? If it does, is the exponent different from 1/2?

accepted.question_text: Prove that the scaling limit of true self-avoiding walk in dimensions greater than 2 is Brownian motion.

evidence.quote: Prove that the scaling limit of True Self Avoiding Walk in d > 2 is Brownian Motion.

accepted.question_text: Construct the nontrivial renormalization-group fixed point for a solid-on-solid interface model with two competing exponentials, at least in the regime where the fixed point is close to a Gaussian one.

evidence.quote: An important open problem is to construct the non-trivial renormalization group fixed point for a solid-on-solid model of an interface with two competing exponentials. This should be doable at least in the regime where this fixed point is closed to a Gaussian one

accepted.question_text: Give a rigorous meaning to the Wulff construction for such interface models.

evidence.quote: An other important problem is to give rigorous meaning to the Wulff construction for such models [DM].

accepted.question_text: Connect perturbative renormalization results for interacting surfaces, such as surfaces interacting with a single impurity, to a constructive analysis.

evidence.quote: There are also perturbative results on the renormalization surfaces interacting e.g. with a single impurity [DDG] which one would like to connect to a constructive analysis.

accepted.question_text: Develop a mathematically firm microscopic theory of quantum non-equilibrium statistical mechanics near equilibrium, including rigorous treatments of the Kubo formula, the Joule effect, and transport theory more generally.

evidence.quote: We remark that the quantum non-equilibrium statistical mechanics remain a widely open subject. An important long term goal for constructive theory should be... to put on a firm mathematical microscopic analysis the Kubo formula and the Joule effect, and more generally transport theory.

accepted.question_text: Carry out the full constructive program for the superconducting BCS phase of interacting fermions in two dimensions, including the intermediate 1/N regime, gluing to earlier scales, and the long-distance Goldstone-boson regime.

evidence.quote: In two dimensions there is a well-defined strategy which should lead ultimately to the complete construction of the BCS2 model, namely the control of the BCS phase at zero temperature

accepted.question_text: For the three-dimensional BCS problem, prove the analog of the two-dimensional convergent-contribution result, namely that the sum of all convergent contributions is analytic in the coupling constant.

evidence.quote: To find the analog of [FMRT1][DR2], namely that the sum of all “convergent contributions” to the theory is analytic in the coupling constant remains in our opinion a major challenge of constructive theory.

accepted.question_text: Develop the theory of Bose-Einstein condensation, either as part of the fermionic BCS program where the bosons are Cooper pairs or as an independent bosonic constructive program.

evidence.quote: Develop the theory of Bose-Einstein condensation. This can be viewed as a piece of the previous BCS program where the bosons are Cooper pairs

accepted.question_text: Extend renormalization analysis beyond convex Fermi surfaces by treating surfaces with flat pieces and-or singular points, including the half-filled square-lattice Hubbard model.

evidence.quote: Treat non-spherical surfaces. After the work on the renormalization of convex surfaces [FKLT][FST], treat surfaces with flat pieces and/or singular points: the regular Hubbard model at half-filling on a square lattice has both these features.

accepted.question_text: Develop a rigorous non-perturbative mean-field theory for condensed-matter models such as the Hubbard model, namely a non-perturbative version of the dynamical mean-field or d = ∞ limit.

evidence.quote: Develop a rigorous non-perturbative mean-field theory for condensed matter, i.e. develop the non-perturbative version of the dynamical mean-field or d = ∞ limit of models such as the Hubbard model

accepted.question_text: Develop the mathematical theory of conduction in quasi-crystals, including proving charge-density-wave generation at low temperature for interacting fermions in one-dimensional quasi-periodic settings and extending the resulting bridge to higher-dimensional models.

evidence.quote: Develop the mathematical theory of conduction in quasi-crystals. In one dimension it is believed that fermions develop a Charge Density Wave instability at small temperature with period equal to the inverse of the density. An interesting goal is to prove the generation of such CDW in a system of interacting Fermions... It would be nice to extend this bridge to other models, in particular in greater dimensions.

accepted.question_text: When Lindstedt series fail to be analytic in the non-analytic KAM setting, determine whether some broader notion of summability, such as Borel summability, still holds.

evidence.quote: In more general cases where the summability of Lindstedt series may fail it is an open question to know if some extended notion of summability, like Borel summability (quite frequent in quantum field theory), may still hold.

accepted.question_text: Prove Arnold diffusion in general a priori stable systems, including those arising from celestial mechanics.

evidence.quote: Using Dyson equation for classical mechanics, Arnold diffusion can be proved in certain a priori stable systems [GGM], but the same question is open in general a priori stable systems such as those arising from celestial mechanics.

accepted.question_text: Explain the origin of intermittency, meaning deviations from Kolmogorov scaling in velocity correlators, in fully developed turbulence.

evidence.quote: However an explanation of the origin of intermittency in the general case of developed turbulence remains one of the main open problems of theoretical hydrodynamics.

accepted.question_text: Extend the constructive results on the Gutzwiller trace formula to longer time evolution.

evidence.quote: Here let us mention the results [CRR] on the Gutzwiller trace formula, that one would like to extend to longer time evolution.

accepted.question_text: Put the heuristic connection between quantum chaos and random-matrix spectra on a mathematically rigorous footing.

evidence.quote: A main challenge is to put the heuristic connection between quantum chaos and the spectra of random matrices on a mathematically rigorous footing.

accepted.question_text: Study the stability of fronts in dissipative equations using renormalization-group methods.

evidence.quote: The major open problems listed in [BK2] are the study of stability of fronts in dissipative equations

accepted.question_text: Extend renormalization-group methods to hyperbolic equations.

evidence.quote: The major open problems listed in [BK2] are... extension of renormalization group methods to hyperbolic equations

accepted.question_text: Study invariant measures for coupled map lattices and the corresponding nonequilibrium phase transitions in which those invariant measures change with the coupling.

evidence.quote: The major open problems listed in [BK2] are... the study of invariant measures for dynamical systems called Coupled Map Lattices [Ka], and of nonequilibrium “phase transitions” in which these invariant measures change as the coupling is varied.

accepted.question_text: Find an inductive rigorous constructive renormalization scheme that is as simple as Polchinski's inductive perturbative renormalization, even in fermionic settings.

evidence.quote: An open problem which could be mentioned along these lines is to find an inductive rigorous constructive renormalization which would be as simple as Polchinski’s induction for perturbative renormalization [P]: even for Fermions, this remains an open problem

accepted.question_text: Develop techniques for gluing together different expansions or different renormalization-group regimes, such as small-coupling and 1/N regimes, in order to treat models with genuinely non-perturbative phases.

evidence.quote: Techniques to glue together different expansions or different regimes of the renormalization group (e.g small coupling/1/N coupling) should be developed. This is a condition to treat many interesting models with “non-perturbative” phases.

accepted.question_text: Develop more general methods for quotienting out or breaking important symmetries, such as gauge symmetry, supersymmetry, and replica symmetry, together with a general theory of non-perturbative Ward identities.

evidence.quote: Many difficult constructive problems involve symmetries which are crucial to their understanding (gauge symmetries, supersymmetry, replica symmetry). One would like to have more general methods to quotient out or break these symmetries, and develop a more general theory of non-perturbative Ward identities.

accepted.question_text: Build a non-perturbative theory of functional integration in non-integer dimensions and explain why constructive analogs of the usual perturbative non-integer-dimensional tools are currently missing.

evidence.quote: Non-integer dimensions is an interesting perturbative tool... that has no constructive analog. One should understand why and build the non-perturbative theory of functional integration in non-integer dimensions.

accepted.question_text: Develop a broader theory of random matrices with non-independent coefficients, especially matrices constrained by geometric structure, so that random-matrix methods become usable in higher-dimensional constructive problems.

evidence.quote: An important progress may come from the understanding of random matrices with non-independent coefficients... Constructivists... may therefore try to develop a more general theory of random matrices, including in particular those with constraints of geometric origin

trace.notes: Mapped the arXiv PDF and identified sections II-VI plus numbered subsections as the main open-problem regions.
Extracted explicit numbered problems from sections III.1, III.3, III.4 and open-problem statements embedded in sections II, III.2, III.5, IV, V, and VI.
Rewrote each candidate into standalone mathematical English while preserving only source-supported model names, ambient dimensions, and stated goals.
Kept distinct items separate when the paper treated them as different programs, and merged only tightly coupled multi-sentence statements into single questions.
Accepted items have page-grounded verbatim evidence and were retained only when the source text itself stated the open problem strongly enough to support a self-contained rewrite.
Saved exact JSON to outputs/parse-paper/constructive-field-theory-and-applications-perspectives-and-open-problems.json and updated outputs/latest.json.
